title: Why Do Over 50 Dogs Keep Jumping Off This Scottish Bridge?
description:
Since the 1960s, more than fifty dogs have leapt from the same fifteen-foot stretch of Overtoun Bridge near Dumbarton, Scotland — always from the right-hand parapet, almost always on dry, sunny days. Built in 1895 for Lord Overtoun, the bridge has earned a grim nickname: the 'Dog Suicide Bridge.'

In 2014, an SSPCA officer proposed a scientific explanation involving mink scent trapped beneath the bridge, invisible to dogs at their eye level. It's a tidy theory — but it doesn't explain the 1994 incident, when a local man threw his infant son from the same spot, convinced the child was the Antichrist, before attempting to jump himself. The baby survived.

Locals call it a 'thin place,' where the boundary between worlds wears thin. No barrier has ever been erected. And disturbingly, some dogs that survive the fall have returned months later to jump again.
